questions: Compared with iteration 1 (mass 0.6 kg, otherwise identical), does mass 0.5 kg raise s-bend progress above 0.26 and hold oval progress at or above 0.47?
Does steering_oscillation rise above about 0.28, and does max_error move above 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend?
Where does the first off-track event occur (track, bend, progress, time)? Please use per-step telemetry if available.
Does the slalom line-loss count or progress change relative to iteration 1 (about 1.0 line-loss events, 0.096 progress)?
Which geometry limit now constrains the controller most: mass, wheel_track, sensor lead or sensor spread?

intent: Single-variable test of mass on the iteration-1 design. Only mass changes, from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Iteration 9 showed that 0.8 kg cost s-bend progress, so this tests the opposite direction to find whether lower yaw inertia improves bend tracking. Everything else matches iteration 1, so any change in score is attributable to mass. Expected: s-bend progress at or above 0.26, oval progress at or above 0.47, and a score at or above about 114. If steering oscillation rises above about 0.3, the mass floor is near 0.6 kg and the remaining gains must come from the controller.
learning: Iteration 9 (mass 0.8) lost score, mainly on s-bend progress (0.26 to 0.16), so heavier mass hurts bend tracking. Iteration 4 combined a lighter mass with other changes and overshot, so the lower-mass direction is not yet isolated. If mass 0.5 raises s-bend progress while holding oval progress, the next step is to test mass 0.4 or to pair the lighter mass with a narrower track. If oscillation rises sharply without a progress gain, mass 0.6 is near optimal and the remaining gain must come from controller changes rather than geometry.
rationale:
Scores so far: iteration 1 = 114.4 (best), iteration 8 = 113.4, iteration 4 = 110.2, iteration 6 = 109.9, iteration 7 = 107.6, iteration 9 = 106.0, iteration 3 = 102.8, iteration 5 = 91.8, iteration 2 = 65.7, iteration 0 = 52.3. Every run has ended off track with zero finishes. Max error is 0.061 to 0.068 m against the 0.06 m off-track floor, while RMS error stays at 0.023 to 0.031 m. The robot tracks well until one excursion takes it over the edge.

The sensor layout is settled. The 5-sensor, 12 mm array at x = ±0.05 m (0.025 m spacing) beat the 7-sensor 16 mm and 5-sensor 8 mm variants. The sensor lead peaks near 0.03 m (0.02 m gave 91.8, 0.04 m gave 109.9). Wheel_track is near its plateau at 0.09 to 0.10 m, since 0.11 cut oscillation but also cut progress. Body width cannot help, because the 0.06 m floor governs the off-track limit.

Mass has now been isolated in one direction. Iteration 9 raised mass from 0.6 to 0.8 kg with everything else at iteration 1, and the score fell from 114.4 to 106.0. Oval progress fell from 0.47 to 0.49 (up, but oval scoring rose only slightly), while s-bend progress fell from 0.26 to 0.16 and slalom changed little. So extra inertia hurts the bends. The reverse direction is untested cleanly: iteration 4 also cut mass to 0.5 but changed radius and length at the same time and overshot. My decision is to test mass 0.5 kg alone on the iteration-1 design, which lowers yaw inertia and should help the bends that the 0.8 kg result hurt. Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.26 and a score near or above 114. The risk is that the lighter robot oscillates more, as iteration 4 did.
